about: Pages to copy by hand for the handwriting-recognition test set. Each page lists what to write; `lines` are the ground truth (LaTeX) a model's transcription is scored against, one per handwritten line. `diagram` describes any drawing the model should describe or export rather than transcribe.

pages.title: Fractions, roots and exponents
pages.tests: nested fractions, radicals, superscripts sitting on fractions

pages.title: Subscripts and superscripts together
pages.tests: indices vs exponents, double subscripts, primes
lines: a_{ij} = a_{ji} \text{ for all } i, j

pages.title: Characters that look alike
pages.tests: 1 l I, 0 O o, z 2, x times, u v, epsilon vs element-of, t +, 5 S, 9 g q

pages.title: Integrals, sums and limits
pages.tests: limits of integration, big operators, dx placement

pages.title: Complex numbers
pages.tests: i vs 1, bars for conjugates, modulus bars, arg, Greek theta

pages.title: A sketch in the complex plane
pages.tests: labels on a diagram; model should describe the drawing, not invent formulas
pages.diagram: Axes labeled Re and Im. A circle centered at 1 with radius 2, with 1, -1 and 3 marked on the real axis and the inside shaded. (As drawn: the shaded region is not labeled.)

pages.title: Matrices and vectors
pages.tests: brackets, alignment of entries, determinants, transpose
lines: \det \begin{vmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{vmatrix} = ad - bc

pages.title: Abstract algebra
pages.tests: group notation, quotients, cong, cyclic groups, mapsto

pages.title: Logic and set notation
pages.tests: quantifiers, negation, set builder, subset vs element, empty set vs phi
lines: A \setminus B = \{ x \in A : x \notin B \}
A \subseteq B \land B \subseteq A \implies A = B

pages.title: Combinatorics
pages.tests: binomial coefficients vs fractions, factorials, piecewise
lines: F_n = \begin{cases} n & n \le 1 \\ F_{n-1} + F_{n-2} & n \ge 2 \end{cases}

pages.title: A small graph
pages.tests: diagram with labels plus a short statement
pages.diagram: Draw K_4: four dots labeled a, b, c, d at the corners of a square, with all six edges (the four sides and both diagonals).

pages.title: A short proof in sentences
pages.tests: prose mixed with inline math; this is the TeX write-up use case
lines: \text{Proof. Suppose } \sqrt{2} = p/q \text{ with } p, q \text{ integers } q \ne 0, \text{ in lowest terms.}
\text{Then } p^2 = 2q^2, \text{ so } p^2 \text{ is even, hence } p \text{ is even. Write } p = 2r.
\text{Then } 4r^2 = 2q^2, \text{ so } q^2 = 2r^2 \text{ and } q \text{ is even too.}

pages.title: A derivation, one step per line
pages.tests: equals signs lined up down the page

pages.title: Scratch work (messy on purpose)
pages.tests: crossed-out steps, arrows, margin notes; the model should ignore what is crossed out
pages.scratch: Write the first line. Then write (x - 1)(x - 6) = 0 and cross it out with one line. Write the correct factoring next to it with an arrow pointing to it. Circle the final answer, and write 'check: 4 - 10 + 6 = 0 ✓' small in the margin.

pages.title: Fast and sloppy
pages.tests: your real speed; write this as quickly as you would when thinking
lines: \int x e^x \, dx = x e^x - e^x + C
